newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel contango widens.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel contango widens.

text.p: The contango which was seen on the physical gas oil market since early this week widened further on Thursday as buyers shifted focus to end-June rather than mid-June cargoes, while many sellers were still seen offering front month cargoes, traders said.

This was illustrated by the two deals seen at $24.80 for June 13-17 lifting and at $25.30 for June 24-28. The former was sold by a US major to a Dutch trader, while the latter was from a European major to a Japanese trader.

The jet fuel market suffered a beating with physical spread widening to 95 cents per barrel, in favour of gas oil, after a 250,000 barrels exchanged hands below the $24-mark for the first time this year.

The first 120,000-barrel cargo was sold by a US trader to a Singapore trader at $23.85 for June 13-17 lifting fob, while the second cargo was traded at $23.90 between a US trader and a Japanese trader for June 13-17 lifting.
"The market hsa been pushed too far (down)," one trader said.

But the gas oil swaps market received a "kick" later on Thursday after earlier weakness on market talk that India might take up to 800,000 tonnes of gas oil in its tender for July delivery, rather than the earlier projected 400,000-600,000 tonnes.
June gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.15/$25.25, up 40 cents from Wednesday.
Traders cited Mobil, Shell, Mabanaft, Tomen, Cargill and Kuwait Petroleum Corp as among the frontrunners for the Indian tender which will be awarded later this evening.
This came despite news of a fire and an explosion at a hydro-desulphurisation unit at Taiwan's Taoyuan refinery, state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp's main production facility for jet fuel.

A CPC source said it was still too early to say if it would have to import more jet fuel as the disruption to output is still being assessed. Another CPC executive said the fire occurred while the unit was being shut for annual maintenance and was doused within one hour.
Brokers said the incident has no effect on the swaps market.
Traders also noted that the offers into the tender were lower than in earlier months.

Sri Lanka was expected to award its middle-distillates import tender to Dutch trader Vitol for June 10-11 delivery with its gas oil offer at five cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes and jet fuel at a 10-cent premium.
